label: Claude Code
description: One conversation with Claude Code, Anthropic's coding agent: three conversations are three nodes. Wire `agent` and `stream` into an AskAgent and talk to it in a Loop; end the loop with a CloseBus on `stream`, which ends this node's part of the run. With no `computer`, Claude Code runs on your machine (a local install only) with your own login, working in `folder`, from your own install of `claude` when there is one on PATH; when there is none, weft installs Claude Code itself, once, into a folder of its own shared by every program on the machine. With a `computer` wired, it is installed and run inside that computer, which a cloud install needs, and it logs in with the connection on `access`. Its card shows what it is doing and a Start over button. What is exposed, and why the rest is not: the permission mode, the model and effort, a system prompt to append, extra folders, the tools it may or may not use without asking, a fallback model, subagents, Claude in Chrome and Remote Control are its settings; flags that would break the conversation weft holds (`--bare`, which skips the subscription login, `--print` formats, `--resume`) are weft's own, set for every turn. Your program's tools reach Claude Code under their plain names, and a tool named like one of its own (`Read`, `WebSearch`, `Agent`, ...) takes that one's place; `ToolSearch` is the one it cannot give up, so a tool of that name is refused when the program is built.

inputs.name: computer
inputs.description: A Computer to run Claude Code in. Left out, it runs on your machine, which only a local install has. Several agents may share one computer.

inputs.name: access
inputs.description: A ClaudeCodeAccess's `access`: your subscription token (on a local install) or an API key. Required with a `computer`. Left out on your machine, Claude Code uses the login already on it.

inputs.name: folder
inputs.label: Folder
inputs.description: The folder Claude Code works in. On your machine it is required, and must exist. In a computer it is a path inside the computer, its home folder when left out.

inputs.name: program
inputs.label: Program
inputs.description: On your machine: the Claude Code program to run, when it is not the `claude` on your PATH or the one weft installs (an install of your own, a version you keep for this). A path on your machine, so it cannot go with a `computer`.

inputs.name: permission
inputs.label: Permissions
inputs.description: What Claude Code may do without asking. `ask`: every request it would put to a person comes out of AskAgent as a question. `accept_edits`: file edits go ahead, the rest asks. `auto`: Anthropic's classifier lets safe actions through and asks about the rest. `plan`: it only plans, and asks before acting on the plan. `dont_ask`: anything not allowed beforehand (`allowedTools`) is refused without asking. `bypass`: nothing asks, nothing is refused; for a computer, which is the wall around it.

inputs.name: model
inputs.label: Model
inputs.description: An alias (`opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`, `fable`) or a model's full name. Left out, Claude Code's own default for your login.

inputs.name: effort
inputs.label: Effort
inputs.description: How hard the model thinks. Left out, Claude Code's default.

inputs.name: streamBy
inputs.label: Stream by
inputs.description: What goes out on `stream`: `message`, one event per whole message, tool use and result, so a run waiting on a long step sleeps; `token`, every piece of text as it is written too, which keeps the run awake while the agent writes.

inputs.name: appendSystemPrompt
inputs.label: Add to the system prompt
inputs.description: Text added after Claude Code's own system prompt, for every turn.

inputs.name: addDirs
inputs.label: Extra folders
inputs.description: Folders besides `folder` Claude Code may read and write.

inputs.name: allowedTools
inputs.label: Allowed without asking
inputs.description: Tools it may use without asking, in Claude Code's own rule syntax (`Bash(git *)`, `Edit`).

inputs.name: disallowedTools
inputs.label: Never allowed
inputs.description: Tools it may never use, in the same syntax.

inputs.name: fallbackModel
inputs.label: Fallback model
inputs.description: A model to fall back on when the chosen one is overloaded.

inputs.name: agents
inputs.label: Subagents
inputs.description: Subagents Claude Code may hand work to, by name: `{ "reviewer": { "description": "Reviews code", "prompt": "You are a code reviewer" } }`.

inputs.name: chrome
inputs.label: Claude in Chrome
inputs.description: Let Claude Code drive Chrome through the Claude in Chrome extension, on the machine it runs on.

inputs.name: remoteControl
inputs.label: Remote Control name
inputs.description: Set, the conversation is also reachable from claude.ai/code and the Claude app under this name (Remote Control), which needs a subscription login.

outputs.name: agent
outputs.description: The agent's handle: wire it into AskAgent's `agent`. Baked: made when the infra is started.

outputs.name: stream
outputs.description: Everything the agent does in this run, as AskAgent sends it. Wire it into every AskAgent of the loop, and into a CloseBus after the loop: the run's part of this node ends when it does.

then.message: ClaudeCode '{id}' runs on the machine weft runs on, which a cloud install does not have; wire a Computer into `computer`.
ClaudeCode '{id}' runs in a computer, where no login is waiting for it; give it a ClaudeCodeAccess on `access`.
ClaudeCode '{id}' works on your machine, so it needs a `folder` to work in.
ClaudeCode '{id}' has a `permission` it does not know; pick one of ask, accept_edits, auto, plan, dont_ask, bypass.
ClaudeCode '{id}' has a `streamBy` it does not know; pick message or token.
ClaudeCode '{id}' runs in a computer, where `program`, a path on your machine, means nothing; leave `program` out, the computer installs Claude Code itself.
